advisor_ref.digest_head:
# Hat wave synthesis — fix-at-loop

Seats run: hat-facts-gaps (opus), hat-user-impact (opus). hat-alternatives
did not run: its transport is a herdr pane (`agy-flash`) and the leader
session is not inside herdr. The plan's inline SMALLER PATH check stands
for that seat.

Reports:
- `.bee/mailbox/job-1794847870557-2201028-1/report-1.md` (facts-gaps)
- `.bee/mailbox/job-1794847872132-2201180-1/report-1.md` (user-impact)

## Accepted

| Finding | Seat | Landed in |
|---|---|---|
| BLOCKER: cross-fe

cells.title: File a fix-at mistake once across features
cells.action: Implement docs/history/fix-at-loop/CONTEXT.md D1. Anchors: in verbs/drivers/close.rs `fn file_fix_at_rows(root: &Path, feature: &str) -> FixAtRows {` and its call `if backlog::backlog_finding_exists(root, feature, &layer, &title) {`; in verbs/backlog.rs `pub(crate) fn backlog_finding_exists(root: &Path, feature: &str, layer: &str, title: &str) -> bool {`. Add a sibling helper in backlog.rs that, per D10, returns the feature of a finding row with this layer and the same crate::verbs::feedback::normalize_title in the CURRENT close epoch (its ts is newer than the newest backlog-closed row with the same normalized title), or None; call it from file_fix_at_rows in place of the per-feature check. After a close, the same mistake files a new row. A skip still counts in rows.skipped; when the owning feature differs from the closing one, the close line's `bee backlog findings --feature <feature>` pointer names the owning feature (anchor: the `(M already there)` line near close.rs:3217). backlog_finding_exists and bee backlog add stay unchanged. Update the doc comments the change makes false only by deleting them; write no new comment. Edit only the existing tests the change forces; the tester cell adds the new ones. Run the related tests and quote the count the filter matched.

truths: A run that closes two features with one mechanizable reflection files one row, and the second close counts it as already there and names the owning feature
After a backlog-closed row with the same title, the same mistake at close files a new row
Two different titles still file two rows
bee backlog add keeps its per-feature dedupe

cells.title: Test fix-at identity at close
cells.action: Contract C1 of docs/history/fix-at-loop/CONTEXT.md. First cite the existing tests that already cover file_fix_at_rows by name, then add only the gap, each test name containing fix_at_identity: (1) a finding with layer fix-at:check and title T under feature A exists, file_fix_at_rows for feature B with a mechanizable mistake titled T files nothing and counts one skip; (2) a different title under feature B files one row; (3) bee backlog add with the same title under a new feature still appends (its per-feature dedupe is unchanged); (4) finding T under feature A, then a backlog-closed row titled T, then file_fix_at_rows for feature B with mistake T files one new row; (5) a whitespace variant of T is treated as T. Show each new test red against the parent commit of fal-1 where the contract changed (tests 1), or state why it passes on both (tests 2, 3). Quote the count the filter matched. No code comments.

truths: fix_at_identity tests exist and pass, with a matched count above zero

cells.title: Fold copies and report open, closed and preamble load
cells.action: Implement D2, D6 and D8 of docs/history/fix-at-loop/CONTEXT.md (D3 is superseded, D4 narrowed by D8). Anchors in verbs/feedback.rs: the backlog ingestion `raw.push(RawCandidate {` under `match resolve_in_scope(&real_root, SRC_BACKLOG) {`, `fn fix_at_row_counts(root: &Path) -> (Option<u64>, Option<u64>) {`, `fn prose_load_value(root: &Path) -> Value {`, `fn prose_load_line(digest: &Value) -> String {`. (1) D2 with D10: during backlog ingestion, a finding or friction row whose (type, layer, normalize_title, close epoch) equals an earlier row's is folded into that row's candidate instead of pushed: the candidate keeps the earliest ts as first_seen and its pain is not summed. The close epoch of a row is the count of backlog-closed rows with the same normalize_title and an older ts. Other row types and other sources are untouched; backlog-closed rows are never folded. So a copy filed after a close stays its own entry and rank still reports the group as recurred. (2) D8: prose_load gains fix_at_check_open, fix_at_architecture_open and fix_at_closed. A distinct (layer, title) of a fix-at finding is closed when a backlog-closed row whose normalize_title equals the finding's normalize_title has a ts newer than the newest finding row of that key; otherwise it is open. Distinct keys are counted, never raw rows; the existing fix_at_check_rows and fix_at_architecture_rows stay raw and unchanged. The printed prose line names the open and closed counts and the preamble size, for example `fix-at: 129 open (110 check, 19 architecture), 1 closed; preamble 8,912 bytes / 151 lines`. (3) D6: prose_load gains preamble_bytes and preamble_lines from the preamble rendered for root by crate::hooks::session_preamble::budget::build_session_preamble_within with PREAMBLE_BUDGET_BYTES as the budget, runtime claude, and no session id or handoff (the number is a snapshot of the current state); when the render panics or root is not a bee project both are null (wrap with std::panic::catch_unwind or check the builder's own fail-open contract first and say which). The digest never fails because of these fields. Edit only the existing tests the change forces (the prose_load_reports_lines_patterns_and_rows_in_object_and_sentence fixture may need new keys); the tester adds the new tests. No code comments. Quote the matched test count.

truths: Eight identical fix-at rows produce one digest entry with the earliest first_seen
A fix-at title with a newer backlog-closed row counts as closed, not open
prose_load carries preamble_bytes and preamble_lines, null on a render failure
The existing raw row counts are unchanged

cells.title: Test the fold, open counts and preamble load
cells.action: Contracts C2 and C4 of docs/history/fix-at-loop/CONTEXT.md. Cite the existing prose_load and rank tests by name, then add the gap. Names containing fix_at_open: (1) three identical fix-at:check rows give one digest entry and fix_at_check_open 1; (2) a backlog-closed row with the same title and a newer ts moves it to fix_at_closed 1 and open 0, and rank lists it as retired; (3) a finding row newer than that close moves it back to open, stays a separate digest entry, and rank reports the group as recurred; (3b) a friction row and a pbi row are never folded. Names containing prose_load: (4) a fixture bee root gives preamble_bytes above 0 and at most 9500 and preamble_lines above 0; (5) an empty directory gives null for both and the digest still succeeds. Show each red on the parent commit of fal-2 where the behavior is new. Quote the matched counts. No code comments.
cells.verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- fix_at_open prose_load

truths: fix_at_open and prose_load tests exist and pass with matched counts above zero

cells.title: Ban Path::strip_prefix and move src sites to named helpers
cells.action: Implement D5 as refined by D9 in docs/history/fix-at-loop/CONTEXT.md. (1) Create packages/bee-rs/clippy.toml with disallowed-methods = [{ path = "std::path::Path::strip_prefix", reason = "..." }]; the reason says: use path_identity::strip_root_lexical when both paths come from one source or are relative, path_identity::relative_to when both are absolute paths read from different sources (it also matches through symlinks and Windows 8.3 short names). (2) In path_identity.rs add pub fn strip_root_lexical(path: &Path, root: &Path) -> Option<&Path> (exactly Path::strip_prefix(...).ok()) and pub fn relative_to(path: &Path, root: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> (plain strip first, then both sides through dunce::canonicalize and strip again; None when neither holds). These two bodies are the only allowed calls, each under #[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]. (3) Move every Path::strip_prefix call under crates/bee/src (21 sites in the listed files; find them with the same probe: CLIPPY_CONF_DIR pointing at the new file, cargo clippy without --all-targets) to strip_root_lexical, keeping each site's Result or Option handling equivalent. A site takes relative_to only when both sides are absolute paths from different sources; leader_check.rs:243, which already does plain then canonical by hand, is one and collapses to relative_to. Do not touch str::strip_prefix, and do not touch crates/bee/tests. (4) The cap lists each site that took relative_to with a one-line reason, and quotes the probe count before (21) and after (0). Run cargo clippy --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings and the related tests. No code comments.
cells.verify: cargo clippy --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings && cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- path_identity leader_check

truths: cargo clippy -- -D warnings is green with clippy.toml in place
No Path::strip_prefix call remains under crates/bee/src outside the two helpers
Writing Path::strip_prefix in src makes clippy print a reason that names both helpers

artifacts.substantive: the disallowed-methods rule with its reason

cells.full_suite_reason: cargo clippy here is the lint rule this cell adds, run once as its own red-to-green proof; the cargo test part is filtered

cells.title: Test the two path helpers
cells.action: Contract C3 of docs/history/fix-at-loop/CONTEXT.md. Add tests whose names contain relative_to: (1) plain match returns the tail for both helpers; (2) a root reached through a symlink (tempdir, std::os::unix::fs::symlink under cfg(unix)) gives None from strip_root_lexical and the tail from relative_to; (3) an unrelated path gives None from both; (4) a path equal to the root gives an empty tail. Show the rule red once: write a throwaway Path::strip_prefix call in a scratch src file, run cargo clippy -- -D warnings, quote the disallowed_methods error naming both helpers, then remove the call; do not commit it. Quote the matched test count. No code comments.

truths: relative_to tests exist and pass
the clippy error text was shown once and names both helpers

cells.title: Say how a landed guard closes its row
cells.action: Implement D7 with D8's verb shape. In expertise/static-rules.md, section `## Show it red, then green`, add a closing step: after the rule is green, close the fix-at row it guards with bee backlog add --type backlog-closed --title "<exact finding title>" --layer <same fix-at layer> --severity P3 --detail "guard: <rule> (<commit>)"; say that a newer finding with the same title reopens it in bee feedback rank. In skills/bee-capturing/references/promotion.md step 2 (`2. Mechanizable?`), add one line pointing to that step. Short sentences, active voice, no new section. Then run bee dev regen so the vendored copies match, and include its outputs in the commit. Last, use the documented command once for real: close the strip_prefix finding (its exact title starts with `lcwr-1 compared absolute paths with a plain strip_prefix`; read it with .bee/bin/bee backlog findings --feature leader-check-windows-paths) with layer fix-at:check and detail `guard: packages/bee-rs/clippy.toml disallowed-methods std::path::Path::strip_prefix (<fal-3 commit>)`, then quote the line of .bee/bin/bee feedback rank that lists it as retired. The knowledge concepts are fal-5's.
cells.verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test pointer_integrity --test instruction_laws && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check

truths: static-rules.md tells the agent to file the backlog-closed row after the rule goes green
promotion.md step 2 points to it
vendored copies match after regen
the strip_prefix finding shows as retired in bee feedback rank
prohibitions: Append to .bee/backlog.jsonl only through bee backlog add, one row

Report PASS or the exact mismatch.
cells.verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test pointer_integrity --test instruction_laws --test rule_index_parity

truths: the parity and pointer tests pass
the documented command uses real flags
